rust_summary: a mod item as a fluid container (`native_item_fluid_tank`), and the item fluid helpers in `native_item_fluids.rs`: `native_item_fluid`, `native_item_fluid_fill`, `native_item_fluid_drain`.
doc_summary: a fluid handler on items (`Capabilities.FluidHandler.ITEM`). `native_item_fluid_tank(item, capacity)` makes a mod item a container with a capacity in millibuckets; what it holds lives in the stack's `minecraft:custom_data` under `horizon_fluid` (`Fluid`, `Amount`), so it is saved, sent to Horizon clients and stacks only with equal contents. `native_item_fluid(stack)` reads one item of a stack (vanilla's buckets are built in: empty, water and lava, a whole bucket or nothing); `native_item_fluid_fill(stack, fluid, amount)` and `native_item_fluid_drain(stack, max)` answer how much one item takes or gives and the single item it becomes, as `IFluidHandler.fill`/`drain` through an `ItemAccess`; the stack given is not changed, so the caller shrinks it by one and hands out the result. They work on any side. Bundles need "hooks": @API:item_fluid_tank@.
